purpose: Show the failure cases that prevent the adversarial test suite from being misread as bridge promotion, bridge invalidation, or edge-case collapse.

counterexamples.counterexample: A coupled interior candidate with declared phi is treated as bridge promotion rather than as a test pass.
counterexamples.why_blocked: Passing the suite admits further bridge development only; it does not promote DENSITY_BRIDGE_001 or RATE_UNIFICATION_001.

counterexamples.counterexample: A failing decoupled endpoint test is treated as invalidation of RT_core.
counterexamples.why_blocked: The failure class only blocks the candidate; it does not modify the formal calculus.

counterexamples.counterexample: A near-tie below-floor candidate is collapsed into either pass or fail without recording ambiguity.
counterexamples.why_blocked: Edge cases must preserve admissibility ambiguity under phi rather than being forced into binary closure.

blocked_readings: A suite pass is not bridge promotion.
A suite failure is not RT_core invalidation.
An edge result is not a binary verdict without recorded ambiguity.
forbidden_inference: The counterexamples do not prove the bridge is impossible.
The counterexamples do not define a completed metric.
The counterexamples do not modify RT_core.

non_claims: Does not prove bridge failure in general.
Does not prove a completed metric is impossible.
Does not assert external physical truth.
